annotations.title: Change a collection's files, title or tags

description:
Edit a collection without republishing (which would create a new collection and abandon its comments and history). `action` is one of: "add" - append new `artifacts` (name, mime, content) and/or `existing_artifact_ids` (already-published files of the same space); files already in the collection are skipped, so it is safe to retry. "reorder" - set the full order: `artifact_ids` must be the FULL current member set, every file once (a partial or unknown-id list is rejected; work from a fresh get_collection). "move" - move `artifact_id` from this collection to `to_collection_id` in the same workspace, carrying its comments, reviews and history; if that empties the source it archives itself (a cross-workspace move is refused - share instead). "rename" - set the collection's `title`; it keeps its id, links, comments, reviews and history, and its revision does not change (a wiki page is renamed in its wiki, a memory through remember). "tags" - replace the collection's tags with `tags` (the full set; new names become labels). Tags decide access: a tag's share links let their holders read it, and a private project limits which members see it. The response names who gains and loses access (members_gain/lose, guests_gain/lose); set `dry_run` to see that without changing anything, and tell the person before a change that does either. Returns a lean ack (revision, or from_revision/to_revision for a move) plus `share_code_holders` when the edit exposes files to a share code - re-read with get_collection if you need the full state. WARNING: adding/moving into a share-coded collection makes those files readable by the code's holders. Refuses archived and memory collections. For a larger or binary file use `kythe add <collection-id> <file>`, which streams bytes off disk - up to 32 MiB per artifact - rather than through the model. The response's `url` is the collection's link (after a move, the file in its new collection) - hand that to a person, not the id.

Over MCP the whole request is limited to 1048576 bytes, and base64 inflates content by 4/3, so roughly 786432 bytes of file is the practical maximum here. Larger content goes over the API or the CLI, which have no such ceiling.

action.description:
action is one of: "add" (add files), "reorder" (set the full member order),
 "move" (move a file to another collection), "rename" (change the title),
 "tags" (replace the collection's tags).

artifactId.description:
move: the artifact to move, and the destination collection (same space);
 collection_id is the source.

artifactIds.description:
reorder: the FULL current member set, every artifact once, in the order you
 want (a partial or unknown-id list is rejected; work from a fresh
 get_collection).

artifacts.description: add: new files to create and append.

content.description:
content carries the artifact bytes (32 MiB max per artifact over the API
 and the CLI). An MCP request is capped far lower - the tool description
 carries that endpoint's real ceiling.

mime.description: mime is the content type; defaults to application/octet-stream.

name.description: name is the artifact's filename-like name, e.g. "bench-results.json".

note.description: note is an optional version note.

collectionId.description: collection_id is the collection to edit (for a move, the SOURCE collection).

dryRun.description: tags: true to report the effect without changing anything.

existingArtifactIds.description: add: references to already-published artifacts of the same space to append.

space.description:
space optionally selects which of your spaces to act in (an id or name
 from list_spaces). Omit it when you belong to a single space.

tags.description:
tags: the full set of tags the collection should carry (labels and
 projects); names not yet in the workspace become new labels.

title.description:
rename: the new title. The collection keeps its id, links, comments, reviews
 and history; the revision does not change.

toCollectionId.description:
to_collection_id is the collection to move the artifact INTO; collection_id
 is the one it leaves. Both must be in the same space.

name: edit_collection

fromRevision.description:
from_revision / to_revision are the source and destination revisions after a
 move.

guestsGain.description:
guests_gain / guests_lose: share links (by label) and tag passwords whose
 holders can now / can no longer read it without an account.

membersGain.description:
members_gain / members_lose: workspace members who can now / can no longer
 see the collection (a private project decides this), by name.

ok.description: ok is true when the edit applied.

revision.description:
revision is the collection's revision after add/reorder, or (unchanged) after
 a rename.

shareCodeHolders.description:
share_code_holders lists share-code labels whose holders can now read a
 newly-added or newly-moved file anonymously (the exposure the edit created).

tagsAdded.description:
tags: what the change does (or would, on a dry run). Tell the person who
 gains or loses access BEFORE you make a change that does either.

url.description:
url is the collection's canonical link - after a move, the file within its
 destination - hand THAT to a person, never the bare id.

title: Change a collection's files, title or tags
